related.name: Taj Madurai Ltd
related.note: Associate company, 26.00% held by the listed entity. Owns the hotel property in Madurai known as Gateway Madurai, which is licensed to OHL under a long-term agreement. Participates in the Business Responsibility initiatives of the listed entity.

related.name: TAL Hotels & Resorts Ltd.
related.note: Joint venture, 21.74% held by the listed entity; an investment company within the IHCL group and the major shareholder in TAL Lanka Hotels Plc and TAL Maldives Resorts Pte Limited. Does not participate in the Business Responsibility initiatives of the listed entity.

related.name: Lanka Island Resorts Ltd
related.note: Associate held indirectly — the wholly owned subsidiary OHL International (HK) Ltd holds 23.08% in it; owns the hotel property Taj Bentota Resort & Spa, Sri Lanka. Its results are included in the subsidiary's accounts.

related.name: The Indian Hotels Company Ltd
related.note: Investing company with significant influence; operates and manages all seven OHL hotels under a Hotel Operating Agreement (Board approval dated May 12, 2017). Salient terms of the arrangement cover basic management fees, reimbursement of expenditures, salaries of deputed staff, project/technical fee, customer loyalty management programmes and other expenses incurred in connection with services rendered under the agreement. All contracts with related parties during FY 2025-26 were at arm's length.

currentContext.expansion: Oriental Hotels discloses no new-hotel project, no room-addition programme and no dated commissioning pipeline of its own in this bundle. Its footprint is unchanged at seven hotels — Taj Coromandel Chennai, Taj Fisherman's Cove Resort & Spa Chennai, Taj Malabar Resort & Spa Cochin, Vivanta Coimbatore, Vivanta Mangalore, Gateway Madurai and Gateway Coonoor — with a total inventory of 825 rooms including 59 suites; three properties are owned and the balance are held under lease and licence arrangements. Capital spending is therefore renovation- and brand-led rather than capacity-led: the MD & CEO states that during the year 'we completed major asset enhancement initiatives across key hotels in the portfolio', which management says have enhanced guest experiences and strengthened competitive positioning, and the Board's Report states the FY 2025-26 outlay towards capital expenditure was ₹3,473.58 Lakhs. The recent portfolio changes were rebrandings rather than builds — Gateway Coonoor was rebranded in August 2024 as part of IHCL's strategic expansion of its Gateway brand, and Gateway Madurai (a 62-acre heritage property owned by associate Taj Madurai Limited and licensed to OHL under a long-term agreement) was rebranded under the Gateway brand in 2024. Forward intent is expressed only at strategy level, through alignment to IHCL's 'Accelerate 2030' strategy of expansion, operational excellence and digital innovation, and to asset optimisation and enhanced portfolio management — none of it carries a project name, a capex quantum or a completion date. The separately supplied 'Capital commitments' named disclosure (page 142, for the year ended March 31, 2026) carries no readable figure: the block is flagged ambiguous with six value lines against one dated period header and no printed unit, so no capital-commitment amount is usable.

risks.risk: Climate change — physical and transition exposure to the hotel estate
risks.note: Named in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Transition risks arise from evolving environmental regulations, a shift in customer preference toward sustainable travel and rising stakeholder expectations on decarbonisation; physical risks — extreme weather events, rising temperatures, water scarcity and resource constraints — may disrupt hotel operations, increase maintenance and insurance costs and affect asset longevity and service continuity. Mitigation is the Climate Strategy embedded within Paathya (IHCL's ESG+ framework, aligned to the Tata Group's Project Aalingana): accelerating renewable energy adoption (solar, wind), modernising facilities with advanced HVAC, energy-efficient lighting and intelligent building solutions, and a Business Continuity and Disaster Response Plan. This bites harder than for a typical company because the assets are coastal and hill properties — Fisherman's Cove on the Bay of Bengal, Taj Malabar on Willingdon Island, Vivanta Mangalore on the Arabian Sea and Gateway Coonoor in the Nilgiris.

risks.risk: Talent management and retention in a service-intensive business
risks.note: Named in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Inability to attract, develop and retain skilled professionals — particularly specialised roles such as chefs, concierge and senior operational leaders — can affect service quality, operational efficiency, guest experience and brand standards, while high attrition or a limited leadership pipeline may disrupt business continuity and growth plans. Mitigation runs through competitive remuneration, career pathways, the Leadership Assessment and Development Centre (LADC), the Talent Identification and Development Initiative (TIDI) and formal succession planning.

risks.risk: Cyber vulnerabilities, concentrated in a third-party property management system
risks.note: Listed first among the Company's key risks in the MD&A risk-governance table, mitigated through cyber risk assessment and Vulnerability Assessment & Penetration Testing (VAPT). The structural feature is that in the ordinary course of business the Company accesses and relies upon the property management system (PMS) maintained and operated by IHCL, so the reservation and guest-data attack surface is largely outside the Company's own control and depends on IHCL's enterprise security posture, which the AR itself describes as 'an ongoing journey'.

Listed as a key risk in the MD&A risk table, mitigated only by 'awareness & scanning of environment' and 'strategic initiatives'. Management separately warns that near-term performance may be affected by geopolitical developments in West Asia and related aviation disruptions, which could temporarily impact select international and corporate travel corridors; the MD & CEO's letter repeats that global economic conditions and West Asia developments warrant continued vigilance. Hotel demand is discretionary and the fixed-cost base is high, so a demand shock transmits quickly to operating leverage in reverse.

risks.risk: Inflation driving up fuel and commodity prices
risks.note: Listed as a key risk in the MD&A risk table (the mitigation text is truncated in the routed extract at 'Development of a…'). Energy, food and utility inputs are the dominant variable cost line for a hotel operator, and management notes that West Asia disruption could keep fuel, logistics and utility costs elevated.

risks.risk: Food safety, hygiene and quality across a food-and-beverage-heavy revenue mix
risks.note: The BRSR classifies food safety as an opportunity rather than a risk, but the MD&A is explicit that comprehensive SOPs and quality assurance are implemented across all stages of food handling, from procurement to service, 'to mitigate risks and ensure consistency', with regular Taj Positive Assurance Model (TPAM) audits covering food safety, fire, electrical and security standards, and strict FSSAI compliance. Because food and beverage constitutes a significant proportion of total revenue and the Company also executes large outdoor catering events for institutional and state guests, a single food-safety incident carries brand as well as operational consequence.

risks.risk: Structural dependence on IHCL for brand, management, systems and people practices
risks.note: Not labelled a risk by the Company, but evidenced throughout the routed text: IHCL operates and manages the hotels and guides strategy as promoter shareholder and operator; the PMS is IHCL's; HR policies, performance management, talent programmes and the myTAJ platform are aligned to or supplied by IHCL; digital initiatives, Project Aarohan, Project Vridhi, Qmin and Tata Neu/NeuPass distribution all sit with IHCL. The Company's brand identities (Taj, Vivanta, Gateway) are licensed rather than owned, and the Gateway rebranding of the Coonoor and Madurai properties was driven by IHCL's brand strategy — so the economics of the operating and licence arrangements, and their renewal, are a durable dependency.

Not disclosed as a risk in this bundle, but structural on the face of the report: the entire business is seven hotels in South India — Chennai (two), Cochin, Coimbatore, Mangalore, Madurai and Coonoor — with no manufacturing or other activity, and the BRSR reporting boundary covers those 7 hotels. A regional demand shock, a state-level regulatory or event disruption, or the loss of any single large property (Taj Coromandel and Vivanta Coimbatore alone account for a substantial share of the 825 keys) has no offsetting geography inside the Company.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
